questions.q: According to the FinOps Foundation's framework, what is the primary purpose of the Inform phase?
options: Negotiating a discount directly with the cloud provider's sales team
Building visibility into current and forecasted spend and attributing it to the right team or project
Shutting down any resource that costs more than a fixed dollar threshold
Writing the Terraform modules that provision new infrastructure
questions.explain: Inform is about seeing spend in real time and allocating it to the team or project that generated it — the foundation everything else in the framework depends on.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say the Optimize phase can't succeed without the Inform phase happening first?
options: Optimize requires a signed contract with a reserved-capacity vendor before it can begin
Optimize is only legally permitted after a fiscal quarter closes
Optimize tools are physically disabled until Inform is marked complete in Azure
A team can't optimize spend it can't see, or hold anyone accountable for spend it can't attribute to an owner
questions.explain: Optimize depends on Inform having already produced trustworthy, attributed cost data — without visibility and attribution, there's nothing reliable to act on.

questions.q: Why does the FinOps Foundation draw Inform, Optimize, and Operate as a circle rather than a one-time, left-to-right project?
options: Because operating well feeds better data back into the next Inform cycle, making FinOps a continuous loop rather than a project with an end date
Because cloud providers require the three phases to be repeated in reverse order each quarter
Because a circle is simply the FinOps Foundation's preferred diagram style, with no operational meaning
Because Optimize and Operate are actually the same phase under two different names
questions.explain: Operating well produces better data for the next Inform cycle, which surfaces new optimization opportunities — the three phases continuously feed into each other rather than ending.

questions.q: Which persona does the lesson say is responsible for actually right-sizing, re-architecting, or shutting down a resource?
options: Finance
The cloud provider's support team
Engineering
Business/Product
questions.explain: Engineering is the persona that holds the hands-on ability to change infrastructure — Finance can identify a problem in a budget, but only Engineering can act on it technically.

questions.q: What does the Business/Product persona contribute to the FinOps loop, according to this lesson?
options: Context on whether a spend increase reflects real value, such as growth tied to revenue, versus genuine waste
The budget and the forecasting numbers used in financial reporting
The ability to write and apply Azure Policy or AWS tag-policy enforcement rules
The dependency graph Terraform uses to plan infrastructure changes
questions.explain: Business/Product supplies the context that tells the other two personas whether a cost increase is a problem or simply the cost of growth they already agreed was worth it.
